subject: general
question: In still water, Rajni can row 135 km in 7.5 hours, while she can row 48 km upstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the current in km/hr?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Still water speed** = 135 ÷ 7.5 = 18 km/hr

**Upstream speed** = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 km/hr

**Speed of current** = Still water speed − Upstream speed

Speed of current = 18 − 12 = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered in **still water** = 135 km

Time taken in **still water** = 7.5 hr

Distance covered **upstream** = 48 km

Time taken **upstream** = 4 hr

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Upstream Speed** (vᵤₚ) = **Speed in still water** (u) − **Speed of current** (v)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/abdf37f760ce03c7b9359b9b33330f164a5df3b267990f73bc344b8d84a42cdc.png] 

⇒ **Speed of Rajni** in **still water** (u) = 135 / 7.5

⇒ u = 18 km/hr

⇒ **Upstream speed** (vᵤₚ) = 48 / 4

⇒ vᵤₚ = 12 km/hr

⇒ According to the formula: vᵤₚ = u − v

⇒ 12 = 18 − v

⇒ v = 18 − 12

⇒ v = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When the boat moves in the same direction as the stream, the effective speed is the sum of the boat speed and current speed: vdₒwₙ = u + v.

Speed of Current (v) from Net Speeds

The current speed can be calculated directly if both downstream and upstream speeds are known: v = (vdₒwₙ − vᵤₚ) ÷ 2.

Still Water Speed (u) from Net Speeds

The speed of the boat in still water is the average of the downstream and upstream speeds: u = (vdₒwₙ + vᵤₚ) ÷ 2.</p
